propositions: The test kills its xdist worker intermittently on macOS py3.13 due to per-test timeout (300s) firing after the unbounded monolithic loop exceeds budget: 91.6s idle, 504.8s under CPU saturation (1.7x past guard).
The test walks 884 renderable units in one function with ~1768 serial pandoc spawns, making per-test cost load-dependent and corpus-size-dependent rather than bounded by construction.
pytest-timeout with thread method calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, killing the worker process outright with no traceback instead of failing the test.
Chunking the equivalence test with fixed-size batches (40 units per chunk) bounds per-test cost and allows xdist to distribute work, eliminating the structural failure mode.
Adding test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit guards against silently dropping units by asserting chunk concatenation equals _renderable_units() with total >= 100.
The byte-identity property is preserved: all 884 units still compared with real pandoc, _EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE remains 1, and no timeout raise or retry marker is introduced.
